correctness.rationale: Invariance applied to arbitrary antiderivatives of continuous functions of \(z\) gives \(\mathbb E[y^2-a\mid z]=0\), hence \(\mathbb E[y^2]=a\). This immediately excludes \(a<0\); for \(a=0\), \(y=0\) almost surely and the exact identity \(L(xy)=y^2-x^2-xyz\) forces \(x=0\), leaving precisely the equilibrium line. For \(a\ne0\), the exact pointwise identity \(LQ=-2az\) yields \(\mathbb E[z\mid Q]=0\). Integrating \(L(zQ)=(y^2-a)Q-2az^2\) gives the covariance identity. Strict positivity for \(a>0\) follows because \(z=0\) almost surely on an invariant compact support would force \(y^2=a\), constant nonzero \(y\), and then unbounded \(x\). Zero means plus nondegeneracy yield both signs of \(y\), \(z\), and \(y^2-a\); periodic continuity gives two crossings. The inspected verifier checks all load-bearing polynomial identities exactly.

value.rationale: The result gives a natural statistical replacement for the exact spherical first integral present at \(a=0\): a shellwise zero-drift law and a strictly positive radial--kinetic covariance for every compact recurrent statistical state. It also completely settles existence of compact invariant probabilities for \(a\le0\) and forces concrete recurrence crossings for \(a>0\), which is meaningful structural information in a classical thermostat/chaotic-flow model.
residual_risks: The theorem does not distinguish the many compact invariant components known for positive \(a\).

final_claim: For the Sprott A/Nosé--Hoover flow \(\dot x=y\), \(\dot y=-x-yz\), \(\dot z=y^2-a\), every compactly supported invariant probability measure satisfies \(\mathbb E[y^2\mid z]=a\), and for \(a\ne0\), \(\mathbb E[z\mid Q]=0\) with \(Q=x^2+y^2+z^2\). For \(a>0\), \(\operatorname{Cov}(y^2,Q)=2a\mathbb E[z^2]=(2a)^{-1}\mathbb E[(LQ)^2]>0\), ruling out single-sphere support and forcing the stated sign/temperature excursions; for \(a<0\) no compact invariant probability exists, while for \(a=0\) these measures are exactly compactly supported probabilities on the equilibrium line.
limitations: Only compactly supported invariant probabilities and periodic-orbit consequences are covered.
The result does not assert ergodicity of the Nosé--Hoover oscillator or classify noncompact invariant measures, KAM tori, or chaotic components.
